channel.title: NewsCenter — Top 5 news of the day — 2026-11-15
channel.description: The five news that matter most today, chosen from Laurent's newsletters. 19 news received.

item.title: 1. Jensen Huang’s downfall puts Nvidia to the test
item.description: Why it matters: Nvidia’s reported $573 billion market-cap decline, leadership controversy, and possible foreign-intelligence investigation create significant risks for the AI industry’s most important company. Jensen Huang, Nvidia’s former CEO and a central figure at the company, is facing revelations about relationships with female employees, while the company investigates a possible foreign intelligence operation. Nvidia’s market capitalization fell by $573 billion in one week, reviving questions about succession and the risk posed by a key executive.

item.title: 2. US air travel disruptions continue after a nationwide ground stop
item.description: Why it matters: Continuing nationwide air-travel disruptions expose critical FAA infrastructure weaknesses and could accelerate a proposed $50 billion modernization effort. Thousands of flights were canceled Saturday after Friday night’s ground stop, and further disruptions are expected. Authorities blame an FAA contractor, and the Transportation Secretary is seeking $50 billion to modernize the systems.

item.title: 3. Agility goes public as the first publicly traded humanoid company
item.description: Why it matters: Agility’s public debut gives investors a new market benchmark for humanoid robotics, despite its modest $1.8 million in prior-year revenue. Agility has gone public on the Nasdaq as the first publicly traded company specializing in humanoid robots, with a pre-money valuation of $2.5 billion. However, it generated just $1.8 million in revenue last year.

item.title: 4. Adobe integrates AI agents into Firefly and Creative Cloud creative workflows
item.description: Why it matters: Adobe’s integration of controllable AI agents into Firefly and Creative Cloud signals a major shift toward delegating complex creative workflows while preserving human oversight. Adobe is introducing new ways to direct the Creative Agent in Firefly and Creative Cloud to handle complex creative tasks while retaining control over the direction and outcome. Users will be able to delegate repetitive tasks, set their preferences, adjust the agent’s plan, and choose which AI models are used.

item.title: 5. OpenAI invites brands to create verified profiles in ChatGPT
item.description: Why it matters: OpenAI’s verified brand profiles could establish a new commercial layer in ChatGPT by enabling brand discovery, mention analytics, and AI-powered shopping agents. OpenAI has invited brands to claim free verified profiles in ChatGPT, track how often they are mentioned, and set up AI agents for shoppers.
